steps.title: DNA and Genetics
steps.body: DNA carries the genetic code that determines an organism's characteristics. Understanding how genes and alleles are inherited allows us to predict the outcomes of genetic crosses using Punnett squares.

steps.title: DNA
steps.body: A long molecule found in the nucleus of cells. It has a double helix structure (two strands twisted around each other). DNA carries the genetic code that controls what characteristics an organism has.

steps.title: Genome
steps.body: The entire genetic material of an organism. The Human Genome Project sequenced the complete human genome, which helps identify genes linked to diseases.

steps.title: Chromosomes
steps.body: DNA is packaged into chromosomes. Human body cells contain 46 chromosomes (23 pairs). Gametes (sex cells) contain 23 chromosomes (one of each pair).

steps.title: Try it yourself

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use the correct letter notation: capital for dominant, lower case for recessive (e.g. B and b) When drawing Punnett squares, put one parent's alleles across the top and the other down the side Always state BOTH the genotype ratio AND phenotype ratio in your answer Remember: polydactyly is DOMINANT (only one allele needed), cystic fibrosis is RECESSIVE (two alleles needed) Carriers have one recessive allele but do NOT show the characteristic (they are heterozygous) You cannot be a carrier for a dominant disorder — if you have the allele, you have the condition Each pregnancy is an INDEPENDENT event — previous children do not affect the probability for the next Sex is determined by the sperm (X or Y), not the egg (always X)
